text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Streaming tail latency p99 spiked above SLA for the us-east cluster (p99=1.9s, target=1.2s). Possible correlated increase in cache miss rate for prefix hash v5 rollout. Investigating.

sre-aaron: seeing same in grafana, p95 also creeping up to ~900ms. Querying redis KPIs and per-shard hitrate now.

eng-kai: any rollout happening on prefix hashing? I recall a canary earlier this morning.

oncall-ashok: I rolled out prefix-hash v5 to 20% at 09:12; metrics looked fine in canary for first 40m. Escalating to 100% at 09:55.

support-jen: customer support stack reports a couple of customers filing slow streaming responses since ~10:05, one with a 20% failure to stream. Not full errors, just long stalls.

infra-lina: grabbing host-level metrics — no CPU/GPU saturation. Network looks normal. Cache eviction rate for kv-prefix caches jumped ~3x around 10:00.

eng-kai: that aligns with a mismatch in prefix salting logic I saw in the rollout diff. If keys remap, cold miss rate spikes and paging increases.

eng-kai: can we confirm the prefix -> bucket mapping change? ashok, can you share the rollout config?

oncall-ashok: paste of the rollout policy: ```canary:20% -> 09:12; ramp:to:100% at 09:55; strategy:replace```. I still have the canary logs.

sre-aaron: running a quick aggregation: cache hit rate (global) dropped from 92% -> 58% between 09:58-10:04. Paging IOPS increased on the p99 hosts.

incident-bot: incident created: INC-2026-330999 — customer-impact: degraded streaming latency; severity: high; responders: @sre-aaron @eng-kai @oncall-ashok.

eng-kai: proposed mitigation: roll back prefix-hash v5 to v4 immediately (rollback is fast, but will require short redistribution window). Alternatively, enable fallback routing to cached-compatible variant (v4) for streaming endpoints.

pm-olivia: customers impacted include three mid-market accounts on dedicated clusters — they currently see degraded p99. We should notify them if >30min.

oncall-ashok: initiating rollback now. Starting traffic switch to v4-compatible buckets at 10:12. Will monitor.

infra-lina: note: when switching, KV rekeying will cause transient cache warmup; expect short-term p95 bump while warm caches refill.

sre-aaron: monitoring tail latency and cache hitback. p99 trending down already to 1.4s at 10:16.

support-jen: filed interim customer messages: "We're aware of a streaming latency issue and are actively mitigating. We'll follow up once resolved."

eng-kai: log snippet from canary shows keys hashed to unexpected namespaces: ```[WARN] prefix-salt-mismatch key=abcd1234 old=nsA new=nsB``` — looks like salt table had an off-by-one in rotation.

eng-kai: root cause hypothesis: a salt rotation in v5 introduced a one-index offset for certain key ranges causing massive remapping and cache invalidations.

oncall-ashok: rollback complete at 10:19; traffic fully on v4 mapping. Running 5 extra minutes of verification.

sre-aaron: p95=420ms, p99=880ms at 10:24 and still improving; cache hitrate back to 89% at 10:25.

pm-olivia: ETA for customer update? recommend: notify at 10:30 with summary + RCA promised within 24h.

eng-kai: agree. I'll start a short postmortem draft and include the diff that caused the salt offset.

infra-lina: we should add a canary test that simulates cold-key remap to measure hitrate regression before full rollout.

sre-aaron: action items I/O: 1) eng to revert code causing salt offset (in PR #5487), 2) infra to add canary workload for cache hit rate, 3) ops to update runbook about safe rollout pacing.

support-jen: logged all affected customer IDs in the incident ticket. Notifying account teams.

incident-bot: INC-2026-330999 status: mitigated -> monitoring.

eng-kai: follow-ups: I'll open the rollback PR and assign to @eng-kai and @infra-lina. Add unit tests around salt rotation math.

oncall-ashok: handing off to day shift SRE for postmortem and customer comms. Thanks all.

sre-aaron: thanks — adding timeline notes to the incident doc.

support-jen: will push a consolidated customer note once we have the RCA.

eng-kai: closing thread once postmortem link is attached.
